message.content:
To retrieve comments for the domain **apple.com** using your `delta_key`, you’ll need to make an authenticated request to the Delta API’s “Get Comments” endpoint. Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to do this, including example code snippets in both **Python** (using `requests`) and **JavaScript** (using `fetch`). Feel free to adapt the examples to whatever language or HTTP client you prefer.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **API Key** | Your unique `delta_key` (e.g., `1234567890abcdef`). |
| **Base URL** | `https://api.delta.com/v1` (replace with the actual base URL if different). |
| **Domain** | `apple.com` – the domain you want to query. |
| **HTTP Client** | Any library that can send HTTPS requests (e.g., `requests`, `axios`, `fetch`). |

> **Tip:** Keep your `delta_key` secret. Never expose it in client‑side code or public repositories.

---

## 2. Endpoint Overview

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| **GET** | `/domains/{domain}/comments` | Retrieve all comments for a specific domain. |
| **POST** | `/domains/{domain}/comments` | Create a new comment for a domain. |
| **PATCH** | `/domains/{domain}/comments/{comment_id}` | Update an existing comment. |
| **DELETE** | `/domains/{domain}/comments/{comment_id}` | Delete a comment. |

> For this tutorial we’ll focus on the **GET** request to fetch comments.

---

## 3. Building the Request

### 3.1. URL Construction

```text
https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments
```

- Replace `apple.com` with the domain you’re interested in.
- If you need to filter or paginate results, add query parameters (see § 3.3).

### 3.2. Headers

| Header | Value | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <YOUR_DELTA_KEY>` | Example: `Bearer 1234567890abcdef` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` | Optional but recommended. |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Required for POST/PATCH/DELETE; optional for GET. |

> **Important:** The `Authorization` header uses the **Bearer** scheme. Do not prefix your key with anything else.

### 3.3. Query Parameters (Optional)

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `page` | integer | `1` | Page number for pagination. |
| `per_page` | integer | `20` | Number of comments per page. |
| `sort_by` | string | `created_at` | Field to sort by (`created_at`, `updated_at`, etc.). |
| `order` | string | `desc` | Sort order (`asc` or `desc`). |
| `status` | string | `all` | Filter by comment status (`approved`, `pending`, `rejected`). |
| `search` | string | `""` | Search term to filter comments. |

> Example:  
> `?page=2&per_page=10&status=approved`

---

## 4. Example Code Snippets

### 4.1. Python (requests)

```python
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://api.delta.com/v1"
DOMAIN = "apple.com"
DELTA_KEY = "1234567890abcdef"   # <-- replace with your real key

url = f"{BASE_URL}/domains/{DOMAIN}/comments"

headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {DELTA_KEY}",
    "Accept": "application/json",
}

params = {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "status": "approved",
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    print("Comments retrieved successfully:")
    for comment in data.get("comments", []):
        print(f"- [{comment['id']}] {comment['content']}")
else:
    print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
```

### 4.2. JavaScript (fetch)

```js
const BASE_URL = "https://api.delta.com/v1";
const DOMAIN = "apple.com";
const DELTA_KEY = "1234567890abcdef"; // <-- replace with your real key

const url = `${BASE_URL}/domains/${DOMAIN}/comments?page=1&per_page=20&status=approved`;

fetch(url, {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": `Bearer ${DELTA_KEY}`,
    "Accept": "application/json",
  },
})
  .then((res) => {
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
    return res.json();
  })
  .then((data) => {
    console.log("Comments retrieved successfully:");
    data.comments.forEach((comment) => {
      console.log(`- [${comment.id}] ${comment.content}`);
    });
  })
  .catch((err) => console.error("Request failed:", err));
```

### 4.3. cURL (Command Line)

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?page=1&per_page=20&status=approved" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer 1234567890abcdef" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

---

## 5. Handling the Response

A successful response will look something like this:

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "total": 57,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "pages": 3
  },
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": "cmt_001",
      "content": "Great product!",
      "author": "John Doe",
      "status": "approved",
      "created_at": "2024-05-01T12:34:56Z",
      "updated_at": "2024-05-02T08:21:00Z"
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `meta.total` | integer | Total number of comments matching the query. |
| `meta.page` | integer | Current page number. |
| `meta.per_page` | integer | Number of comments per page. |
| `meta.pages` | integer | Total pages available. |
| `comments[]` | array | List of comment objects. |
| `comments[].id` | string | Unique identifier for the comment. |
| `comments[].content` | string | Comment text. |
| `comments[].author` | string | Author name or ID. |
| `comments[].status` | string | Status (`approved`, `pending`, `rejected`). |
| `comments[].created_at` | string | ISO‑8601 timestamp of creation. |
| `comments[].updated_at` | string | ISO‑8601 timestamp of last update. |

> **Note:** If you hit a rate limit or receive an error, check the `response.headers` for `x-rate-limit-remaining` and `x-rate-limit-reset`.

---

## 6. Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `401 Unauthorized` | Wrong or missing `delta_key`. | Verify the key and ensure it’s prefixed with `Bearer `. |
| `404 Not Found` | Domain doesn’t exist or endpoint typo. | Double‑check the domain spelling and endpoint path. |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Exceeded rate limits. | Wait until `x-rate-limit-reset` time or reduce request frequency. |
| Empty `comments` array | No comments match filters. | Remove filters or adjust `status`/`search` parameters. |
| Unexpected JSON structure | API version mismatch. | Confirm you’re hitting the correct API version (`/v1`). |

---

## 7. Next Steps

1. **Test the GET request** using one of the snippets above to confirm you can retrieve comments.
2. **Explore pagination** by incrementing the `page` parameter until you reach the last page (`meta.pages`).
3. **Try filtering** with `status=pending` or `search=refund` to see how the API narrows results.
4. **Create a comment** (POST) or **update/delete** a comment (PATCH/DELETE) to learn the full CRUD flow.

---

## 8. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

| Action | Method | Path | Example |
|--------|--------|------|---------|
| Get comments | GET | `/domains/{domain}/comments` | `GET https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments` |
| Create comment | POST | `/domains/{domain}/comments` | `POST https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments` |
| Update comment | PATCH | `/domains/{domain}/comments/{comment_id}` | `PATCH https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments/cmt_001` |
| Delete comment | DELETE | `/domains/{domain}/comments/{comment_id}` | `DELETE https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments/cmt_001` |

---

### Final Thought

Once you’ve verified that the GET request works, you can automate comment retrieval, integrate it into dashboards, or trigger alerts based on comment status changes. Happy coding!
